quote: Gegeben ein Faktor vom $n^{\text{ten}}$ {+Grad+} [-Grade-] einer Covariante von hoher Ordnung. Gesucht alle {+zugehörige+} [-Form-] Grundformen $f=a_x^n$. d.h. Ueber-mehrdeutige Beziehung[?] zwischen Grundform und Covariante.
english: Given a factor of degree n of a covariant of high order. Sought: all associated ground forms $f=a_x^n$, i.e. on the many-valued relation between ground form and covariant.
topic: A list of research topics and problems on binary forms, covariants, invariants, the principle of special position, and the three-body problem.

triage.modern_statement: Take a covariant map C: S^n(C^2) → S^m(C^2) of binary forms of degree n, such as the Hessian or another transvectant of high order m. Suppose you are given a degree-n factor of a value C(f), or more simply the value itself. The problem is to describe every ground form f = a_x^n consistent with that data. In modern terms, this asks for the fibres of the covariant map and how many points they contain: is the map injective or birational onto its image, or finite of some degree d > 1, and can f be reconstructed from C(f)? Hilbert's phrase 'mehrdeutige Beziehung' points to the case where the correspondence between ground form and covariant is many-valued.
triage.answered_by: There is no general answer for arbitrary covariants. The best-studied special case is the Hessian covariant. Ciliberto and Ottaviani, 'The Hessian map' (arXiv 2006.07213), prove that the Hessian map of binary forms is birational onto its image, so a general binary form can be recovered from its Hessian. They cover ternary forms in arXiv 2406.05382 (Doc. Math. 31, 2026). A related paper (arXiv 2307.10415) shows that for binary cubics the correspondence is 2-to-1 (étale of degree 2), which is a genuinely many-valued case. Separately, Abdesselam and Chipalkatti studied covariants of binary forms linked to Hilbert (arXiv 1203.4761), but this is not shown to be the same question.

evidence.claim: For binary forms, the Hessian map h_{d,1} is proved birational onto its image. A general binary form f therefore has no second form f' with the same Hessian.
The Hessian map is birational onto its image for ternary forms of degree d ≥ 4 with d ≠ 5. The abstract says the analogous result for binary forms was proved in an earlier paper.
For binary cubics with distinct roots, the restriction of the Hessian correspondence H_{3,1} is étale of degree 2. So the ground form is not uniquely determined by this covariant.
The ternary Hessian result was published in Documenta Mathematica 31 (2026).
A closely related reconstruction problem, recovering a form from its invariants, is still being studied. For binary forms it has reconstruction algorithms by Mestre and Noordsij.

triage.why: The note is short and gives no particular covariant, so I read it as the general problem of inverting covariant maps of binary forms, meaning describing their fibres. This is not among Hilbert's 23 published problems or the 24th problem, and I found no source that traces it back to this notebook entry. The Hessian case has been settled recently: such maps are generically birational for higher degrees and 2-to-1 for cubics, and the work is ongoing (2020–2026). That shows the theme is active. I found no general result for arbitrary covariants. I also found nothing on the specific version Hilbert wrote down, where only a degree-n factor of a high-order covariant is given. My search budget ran out before I could check older literature (for example 19th-century work on forms with a given Hessian), so the verdict and its attribution are uncertain.
